title: Evaluation of Photosynthetic Behaviors by Simultaneous Measurements of Leaf Reflectance and Chlorophyll Fluorescence Analyses
protocol: Soak Arabidopsis thaliana seeds in sterilized deionized water.
Incubate the soaked seeds for 2 days at 4 °C in the dark.
Place approximately four imbibed, cold-treated seeds onto the soil surface using a micropipette.
Incubate the planted pots in a growth chamber with a 16 h light (120 μmol photons m–2 s–1) and 8 h dark period at 22 °C and 20 °C, respectively.
Thin other seedlings after germination to grow one plant per pot.
Incubate the plants in the growth chamber for an additional 4 weeks.
Prepare at least five pots.
Use the youngest, fully-opened mature leaf for photosynthesis measurements.
Attach a 10 cm² steel plate with a 1 cm diameter hole onto the custom-made sample stage.
Position thin fiber probes for measuring chlorophyll fluorescence and leaf reflectance closely together to measure signals from the same leaf position.
Fit the two probes tightly together and wrap them with plastic tape.
Clip the taped probes onto the sample stage using a coaxial lens holder.
Position the probes vertically to the leaf surface.
Attach a biforked light guide made of glass fibers to the halogen light source.
Irradiate the sample stage from both directions at angles of approximately 45°.
Adjust the light source so that light uniformly illuminates the sample stage without casting shadows.
Enter the dark room to avoid light detection other than actinic light.
Turn off all weak-green lights before measurements begin.
Place a test leaf on the leaf holder of the sample stage in darkness.
Press the leaf against a steel plate on the stage (black square).
Turn on the PAM and irradiate the leaf with measuring light.
Confirm chlorophyll fluorescence intensity values using PAM controlling software.
Adjust the system so that the fluorescence intensity measures approximately 100 units.
Measure the distance between the probe and the leaf.
Fix the adjuster, and record the value of the distance.
Turn off the measuring light.
Remove the test leaf from the sample stage.
Set a light quantum meter at the position where the sample leaf would be placed.
Irradiate light from the halogen light source and measure the intensity.
Determine which positions of the light source dial generate intensities of 30, 60, 120, 240, and 480 μmol photons m–2 s–1.
Measure a reflection standard.
Place a white plate as a reflectance standard at the position of the leaf sample.
Turn on a spectral radiometer.
Adjust the detection strength of the radiometer to avoid saturation.
Record spectral reflectance between 450–850 nm at 1 nm intervals under illumination with 30, 60, 120, 240, and 480 μmol photons m–2 s–1.
Transfer the Arabidopsis plant from the grown chamber to the controlled dark room with the same temperature and humidity as that of the growth chamber.
Incubate the plant for 1 h in the dark at 22 °C.
Place the dark-adapted whole plant on a lab jack under the sample stage.
Fix the sample leaf to the leaf holder with the leaf surface perpendicular to the detection probes.
Turn on the PAM and start recording the curve.
Turn on the measuring light, and wait approximately 30 s for the curve to respond.
Give a saturated pulse of 4000 μmol photons m–2 s–1 for 0.8 s from the PAM.
Obtain the highest value of the spike in the curve with increased fluorescence intensity.
Calculate the maximum quantum yield of PSII in the dark (FV/FM).
Turn on the halogen lamp as the external light source with the measuring light on after recording FM.
Irradiate the leaf sample with the weakest light (30 μmol photons m–2 s–1).
Turn on the spectral radiometer at the same time to monitor the leaf reflectance.
Wait for 20 min or longer for the photosynthetic reaction to reach steady state under the light conditions.
Supply a saturating pulse at intervals of 1 min during illumination with actinic light.
Record the data of FM′ at 20 min after turning on the actinic light.
Take leaf reflectance data by averaging 10 scans at an optimized integration time, with dark current subtraction.
Calculate the quantum yields of PSII photochemistry (ΦPSII) using the equation ΦPSII = (FM′ - FS) / FM′.
Estimate the linear electron flux (LEF) from the PSII reaction center as LEF = The irradiance intensity of the actinic light × ΦPSII × 0.5 × 0.84.
Calculate NPQ, which can be expressed as thermal dissipation using the equation NPQ = (FM - FM′) / FM′.
Using spectral data acquired with a radiometer under the same light conditions, calculate the leaf reflectance ratio as Reflectance ratio = Rleaf / Rstandard.
Calculate PRI from reflectance at 531 nm and 570 nm.
Turn off the actinic light after acquiring Fs and leaf reflectance.
Monitor chlorophyll fluorescence by PAM for 10 min in darkness.
Provide a saturating pulse at intervals of 1 minute during dark relaxation.
Obtain ten FM′′ values from saturation pulses under dark conditions.
Save data of FM′′ at 2 minutes and 10 minutes after turning off the light.
Turn on actinic light to an intensity of 60 μmol photons m–2 s–1.
Repeat a light adaptation for 20 min followed by dark relaxation for 10 min with pulsing saturation light every minute.
Record all data as described in previous steps.
Increase irradiance intensity sequentially to 120, 240, and 480 μmol photons m–2 s–1.
Estimate the qE fraction using FM′′ after 2 minutes of dark adaptation.
